facts.statement: Richard Owen named the species Pterodactylus validus in 1870 based on a thirty-centimeter-long partial wing finger phalanx found in the Purbeck Limestone of Britain.
facts.quote: In 1870 Richard Owen named Pterodactylus validus based on holotype NHMUK 40653, a thirty centimeter long partial wing finger phalanx from the Purbeck Limestone (Britain), identified as that of a pterosaur.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley obtained a vertebra and a lower jaw from a quarry near Langton Matravers in late December 1868.
facts.quote: In late December 1868 Seeley had obtained a vertebra and lower jaw (catalogued CAMSM J.5340 and J.5339 respectively) from a quarry near Langton Matravers

facts.statement: In 1875, Harry Govier Seeley erected the genus Doratorhynchus for the species validus after re-identifying a previously classified tail vertebra as a cervical vertebra.
facts.quote: In 1875, he concluded that the remains were conspecific with P. validus (he re-identified the vertebra he had previously considered a caudal as belonging to the cervical region), erecting a separate genus name to the species: Doratorhynchus

facts.statement: The genus name Doratorhynchus is derived from Greek words meaning "lance" and "snout," referring to the shape of the jaw.
facts.quote: Doratorhynchus, from Greek dory, "lance" and rhynchos, "snout", referring to the jaw form

facts.statement: Howse and Milner assigned the lower jaw specimen to the genus Gnathosaurus and the vertebra to an indeterminate ctenochasmatid.
facts.quote: They assigned CAMSM J.5339 to Gnathosaurus as G. macrurus and CAMSM J.5340 to an indeterminate ctenochasmatid.

facts.statement: The re-identified cervical vertebra indicated that forms with very long necks existed in the Late Jurassic (Tithonian) or Early Cretaceous (Berriasian).
facts.quote: Más tarde se hizo claro que la vértebra, interpretada como una caudal por Seeley, era una vértebra cervical e indicaba que formas de cuellos muy largos ya existían a finales del Jurásico (Titoniense) o principios del Cretácico (Berriasiense).

facts.statement: It was suggested that Doratorhynchus was a basal member of the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: It was suggested that Doratorhynchus was a basal member of Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Doratorhynchus is recorded as the Late Jurassic to the Cretaceous.
Doratorhynchus is classified within the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
The Paleobiology Database lists Azhdarchidae as the parent group for Doratorhynchus.

rejected.statement: In 1995, researchers Stafford Howse and Andrew R. Milner concluded that Doratorhynchus is a nomen vanum because the original wing phalanx was not diagnostic enough to support a separate genus.
rejected.quote: However, in 1995 Stafford Howse and Andrew R. Milner concluded that Doratorhynchus is a nomen vanum because they noted that the phalanx was not diagnostic enough anyway and only assignable to Pterodactyloidea incertae sedis.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'concluded that Doratorhynchus is a nomen vanum because'
